description: Composite figure with four Thermo-Calc/CALPHAD equilibrium phase-fraction diagrams, one per alloy: (a) 9Al-20Mn-1C, (b) 9Al-30Mn-1C, (c) 12Al-20Mn-1C, (d) 12Al-30Mn-1C (per caption). Every panel plots "Amount of all phases [mol]" (y-axis, 0.00-1.10, 0.05 grid) against "Temperature [°C]" (x-axis, 0-1300, 100 °C ticks) and carries an inset legend naming phases: FCC_A1, BCC_A2, KAPPA_E21 in (a); FCC_A1, BCC_2SL, LIQUID, KAPPA_E21, BCC_A2 in (b) and (d); BCC_A2, FCC_A1, KAPPA_E21, LIQUID, BCC_2SL in (c). Curve colours are not consistent between panels. In (a) and (b) FCC_A1 climbs to a 1.00 mol plateau between roughly 800 and 1050 °C then falls to about 0.75 mol at 1300 °C, while BCC_A2 and KAPPA_E21 disappear near 750 °C and about 520 °C. In (c) and (d) a BCC_2SL curve instead reaches about 0.80 mol over roughly 500-800 °C (c) and 400-600 °C (d), collapsing near 830 °C in (c) before FCC_A1 rises to about 0.72 mol near 1000 °C. The figure's argument is this reversal: austenite (FCC_A1) is more stable at 800 °C than at 1150 °C in the 9Al alloys and the opposite in the 12Al alloys. No numeric data labels are printed on any curve.

subfigures.description: Equilibrium phase-amount vs temperature diagram for 9Al-20Mn-1C (per caption). Legend: FCC_A1, BCC_A2, KAPPA_E21. FCC_A1 (blue) rises from about 0.07 mol at 0 °C to a flat 1.00 mol plateau (roughly 800-1050 °C) then falls to about 0.75 mol at 1300 °C; BCC_A2 (red) starts near 0.73 mol and reaches zero near 750 °C with a small local maximum near 500-550 °C; KAPPA_E21 (green) stays near the 0.20 mol line to about 400 °C then falls to zero by about 800 °C.

Phase-amount vs temperature diagram for 9Al-30Mn-1C. Legend: FCC_A1, BCC_2SL, LIQUID, KAPPA_E21, BCC_A2. A curve labelled BCC_A2 starts near 0.60 mol at 0 °C and vanishes near 500 °C; FCC_A1 rises from about 0.20 mol to the 1.00 mol plateau (roughly 800-1050 °C) then declines to about 0.75 mol at 1300 °C; KAPPA_E21 lies near 0.20 mol and falls to zero near 520 °C; a BCC_2SL curve is labelled near 0.20 mol at the lower right. The last x-axis tick label is cropped ('130').

Phase-amount vs temperature diagram for 12Al-20Mn-1C. Legend: BCC_A2, FCC_A1, KAPPA_E21, LIQUID, BCC_2SL. BCC_A2 falls from about 0.65 mol at 0 °C to zero near 520 °C; BCC_2SL rises and plateaus near 0.80 mol between about 500 and 800 °C, then drops steeply to zero near 830 °C; FCC_A1 then rises steeply to about 0.72 mol near 1000 °C and declines slowly to 1300 °C; KAPPA_E21 is flat near 0.20 mol up to about 800 °C before decaying.

Phase-amount vs temperature diagram for 12Al-30Mn-1C. Legend: BCC_2SL, FCC_A1, LIQUID, KAPPA_E21, BCC_A2. A curve labelled BCC_2SL rises to about 0.80 mol plateau between roughly 400 and 600 °C and then declines; KAPPA_E21 sits near 0.20 mol up to about 300 °C and then decreases; FCC_A1 is labelled near 0.72 mol at about 1000 °C; the low-fraction (<0.15 mol) curves at low temperature and the high-temperature branch identities between about 1100 and 1300 °C cannot be assigned unambiguously at the supplied resolution.

observations.observation: All four panels are equilibrium phase-amount vs temperature curves with x-axis 'Temperature [°C]' spanning 0-1300 °C (100 °C major ticks) and y-axis 'Amount of all phases [mol]' spanning 0.00-1.10 in 0.05 steps.
The caption assigns panel (a) to 9Al-20Mn-1C, (b) to 9Al-30Mn-1C, (c) to 12Al-20Mn-1C and (d) to 12Al-30Mn-1C.
Panel (a)'s legend lists only three phases - FCC_A1, BCC_A2 and KAPPA_E21 - whereas (b), (c) and (d) additionally include BCC_2SL and LIQUID.
In (a) and (b) the FCC_A1 curve rises to a flat maximum at 1.00 mol that extends from roughly 800 °C to roughly 1050 °C, then decreases to about 0.75 mol at 1300 °C.
In (a) BCC_A2 starts near 0.73 mol at 0 °C and falls to zero near 750 °C, while KAPPA_E21 stays near the 0.20 mol gridline up to about 400 °C and vanishes by about 750-800 °C.
In (c) the BCC_2SL phase reaches a plateau near 0.80 mol between about 500 and 800 °C and drops steeply to zero near 830 °C, after which FCC_A1 rises and peaks near 0.72 mol at about 1000 °C.

Curve colours are not consistent across the four panels (FCC_A1 is drawn blue in (a)/(b) but red-pink in (c)/(d); BCC_A2 is red in (a)/(b) but drawn in a different colour in (c)/(d)), so each panel's inset legend must be used for phase identification.
Only axis tick labels and phase-name labels (FCC_A1, BCC_A2, KAPPA_E21, BCC_2SL, LIQUID) are printed; no numeric data labels or uncertainty values appear on any curve.

The citing text states that the austenite amount for 9Al-20Mn and 9Al-30Mn (Fig. 12(a),(b)) indicates more stability at 800 °C than at 1150 °C, whereas for 12Al-20/30Mn-1C the situation was reversed (Fig. 12(c),(d)).
The citing text interprets this panel-to-panel reversal as justifying 'the phase propensity to transform during tempering in 12Al alloys'.
Each panel carries a small red triangular logo/watermark at its lower-left corner, outside the plotted data area.

measured_quantities: phase volume fraction (from phase amount vs temperature curves)
unreadable_items: panel (b): last x-axis tick label cropped (reads '130' instead of 1300 °C)
panel (d): low-fraction curves below about 0.15 mol at low temperature cannot be unambiguously assigned to FCC_A1 vs BCC_A2
panel (c) and (d): identity of the high-temperature branches between about 1100 and 1300 °C (BCC_2SL vs BCC_A2 vs FCC_A1) is only partly resolved
panel (b): the BCC_2SL and LIQUID curves are only weakly traceable at the printed resolution
all panels: no numeric values printed on curves, so all quoted amounts are read from the nearest gridline only
